title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction: This page sets up how Euler extends his parameter method for the calculus of variations from one independent variable to two. A surface is given by z = z(x,y). Euler writes the two partial increments as dx(dz/dx) and dy(dz/dy); the parentheses are his notation for partial derivatives. To compare the surface with all neighbouring surfaces (§18), he introduces an auxiliary parameter t, so that z becomes z(x,y,t). Setting t=0 gives the original surface, and infinitely small t gives the neighbouring ones. Because x and y do not depend on t, dx and dy are never mixed with dt. Only z receives a third kind of increment, dt(∂z/∂t); in modern terms this is the first variation δz = (∂z/∂t)|_{t=0}·dt. In §19 a function V(x,y,z) with dV = L dx + M dy + N dz is varied with respect to t alone. The next page puts dx = dy = 0 and obtains ∂V/∂t = N ∂z/∂t, which is the chain rule; Euler calls such expressions the 'first kind'. This is the groundwork for later sections. There he treats V that depend on the partial derivatives p, p', q, ... (the 'second kind') and derives the Euler–Lagrange equation for double integrals ∫∫Z dx dy.
errors: No mathematical errors. One restrictive assumption: x and y are held fixed (independent of t), so only vertical variations of z are allowed and the domain itself is not varied. This is legitimate for deriving the interior equation, but it excludes variable-boundary problems in two dimensions.
Minor Latin agreement slip: 'quae ... abeant ... complectatur' switches between plural and singular. Running-head misprint 'VARIATINVM' for 'VARIATIONVM'.

ideas.what: Embedding the extremal surface in a one-parameter family z(x,y,t) and defining the variation as the t-derivative at t=0
ideas.modern_name: First variation via a one-parameter family of admissible functions (Gateaux-type derivative)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E420, 1771/72, and related papers of that period). It is often presented as Euler's reinterpretation of Lagrange's δ-method.
ideas.where_published: E420 itself (Novi Comm. Acad. Petrop. 16); Opera omnia I.25, discussed in Carathéodory's introduction

ideas.what: Parenthesis notation for partial derivatives, (dz/dx), with increments dx(dz/dx), dy(dz/dy), dt(dz/dt)
ideas.where_published: Institutiones calculi differentialis / integralis and many Euler papers

ideas.what: Variation of V(x,y,z) with respect to t alone: δV = N δz
ideas.modern_name: Chain rule for the variation of a function of the dependent variable

ideas.what: Programme to extend the variational calculus to functions of two variables, i.e. double integrals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1760–61, minimal surfaces); Euler E420 for a systematic treatment
ideas.where_published: Lagrange, Misc. Taurinensia II; Euler E420 §§16 ff.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely definitional setup: the parameter t, partial increments and the chain rule. All of it is the well-known content of E420, documented in the Opera omnia I.25 commentary and in standard histories of the calculus of variations.
transcription_corrections: The running head is printed 'VARIATINVM' (a misprint in the original for VARIATIONVM); the transcription preserves it correctly.
'profiſiſcuntur' matches the hyphenated print 'profi-ſiſcuntur' (read: proficiscuntur); otherwise the transcription agrees with the image.
